## Importing transcribed compass points and tree measurements

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
por_compass_df<-read_excel("C:/Users/showa/Documents/GitHub/Apiary_LRR/Poria_survey_70s.xlsx", sheet = "Poria_compass_points", range = "A1:AC83", col_names = TRUE)

#subset four compass points for testing
compass_test<-por_compass_df[1:4,]

#first change "C" Y_1, Y_2, Y_3, Y_4 to "0"

#then convert chain grid to computer grid
#compass_test$comp_X_1 <- (-(compass_test$X_1 /2))+17 
#Repeat for X_2, X_3, X_4

#compass_test$comp_Y_1 <- (compass_test$Y_1 + 10) /2
#Repeat for Y_2, Y_3, Y_4

#convert Dist_1-4 from ft to grid units
#compass_test$comp_Dist_1 <- compass_test$Dist_1 /132
#repeat for 2-4

#convert azimuth to radians? or will sin cos tan work with degrees

#see this post for converting bearing and distance to coordinates

#https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22064611/how-to-draw-rotated-axes-in-r/22067400#22067400

get.coords <- function(a, d, x0, y0) {
  a <- ifelse(a <= 90, 90 - a, 450 - a)
  data.frame(x = x0 + d * cos(a / 180 * pi), 
             y = y0+ d * sin(a / 180 * pi))
}

rotatedAxis <- function(x0, y0, a, d, symmetrical=FALSE, tickdist, ticklen, ...) {
  if(isTRUE(symmetrical)) {
    axends <- get.coords(c(a, a + 180), d, x0, y0)    
    tick.d <- c(seq(0, d, tickdist), seq(-tickdist, -d, -tickdist))      
  } else {
    axends <- rbind(get.coords(a, d, x0, y0), c(x0, y0))
    tick.d <- seq(0, d, tickdist)
  }
  invisible(lapply(apply(get.coords(a, d=tick.d, x0, y0), 1, function(x) {
    get.coords(a + 90, c(-ticklen, ticklen), x[1], x[2])
  }), function(x) lines(x$x, x$y, ...)))
  lines(axends$x, axends$y, ...)
}

```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
